name: Hollow cheeks via chewing then fat loss
lead: "Hollow cheeks via chewing then fat loss" refers to a looksmaxxing approach that combines masseter-focused chewing with reducing body and facial fat, in order to show cheekbone and jaw structure. Proponents describe hollow cheeks as the shadowed area below the cheekbones, produced by bone, muscle and the amount of soft tissue [1][2].

No published trial was found that tests chewing followed by fat loss for cheek hollowing. Medical literature in this area concerns facial fat loss from aging and lipodystrophy, and treatments such as fillers and fat grafting to restore cheek volume [3][4][5][6]. Wikipedia notes the buccal fat pad contributes to cheek hollowing, but it describes no chewing-based method [7].

paras: Looksmax.org members describe two broad sources of hollow cheeks: those formed by zygomatic bone projection and those formed by the masseter muscle and jaw angle, with lighting changing how pronounced they appear [2]. In threads on the topic, members also point to a low level of facial fat as a precondition, and some ask whether hollow cheeks can be achieved without dieting [1].
Others dispute the goal. One thread argues hollow cheeks can look overly gaunt and that cheek dimples with a thin fat layer look better [8].

No studies found. Related medical literature is about restoring lost cheek volume: reports on microliposuction and fat transplantation in the aging face [3], collagen fillers used to augment hollow cheeks [4], reconstruction in partial lipodystrophy where extremely hollow cheeks are a feature [5], and a corrective surgery for hollow cheeks [6]. These address volume replacement, not chewing or deliberate fat loss.

Wikipedia describes the buccal fat pad as a deep cheek fat mass that contributes to hollow cheeks and the nasolabial fold, but not to jowls [7]. It lists proposed roles in suckling and as a gliding pad for chewing muscles [7]. It does not discuss whether chewing changes cheek shape.

lore.intro: Hollow cheeks are a frequent topic on looksmax.org, with members describing multiple routes to them and disagreeing about how desirable they are [1][2][8].

claims.claim: Hollow cheeks come from bone and masseter structure, with fat loss revealing them.
claims.believers: A member's guide describes zygomatic projection and masseter muscle as the two main causes, with lighting accentuating the effect [2]. Others say leanness is needed, and a member in another thread says cheeks hollow only when cutting weight [1].
claims.experts: No published studies have tested whether chewing combined with fat loss produces cheek hollows. Medical sources describe facial fat loss in aging and lipodystrophy and ways to replace it [3][5].

claims.claim: Overly hollow cheeks can look gaunt, and a thin fat layer may be preferable.
claims.believers: A looksmax.org thread argues that some facial bone visibility with a subtle fat layer, plus cheek dimples, looks better than very hollow cheeks [8].
claims.experts: Surgical and filler literature treats hollow cheeks as a sign of facial volume loss that may be corrected with fillers or fat grafting [3][4].

card.summary: Chew for the masseter, lean out for the cheeks; popular in forums, but no studies test the combination.
card.note: No trial found for chewing plus fat loss; medical literature on hollow cheeks concerns volume restoration.

quick.overview:
This approach pairs chewing exercises aimed at the masseter with weight and facial fat loss, in the hope of showing cheekbones and a hollow below them.

Forum members disagree about the look itself, and no clinical study of the combination was found.
quick.mechanism: Believers say hollows come from cheekbone projection, jaw angle and masseter size, which become visible when facial fat is low. Wikipedia notes the buccal fat pad also contributes to cheek fullness.
quick.risks: No harms were documented for the combination in the sources reviewed. Medical literature associates very hollow cheeks with aging or lipodystrophy, conditions treated with volume restoration.
